description: The bar chart illustrates a comparison of Accuracy (%) and Token Count across three methods—CoD, CCoT, and CoUT—based on the paper “Efficient Reasoning via Chain of Unconscious Thought.” The left y-axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)” and ranging from 70 to 100, measures performance accuracy, while the right y-axis, labeled “Token Count” and ranging from 0 to 800, measures computational cost. The x-axis lists the three methods, each represented by two bars: one for accuracy (left-side scale) and one for token count (right-side scale). For CoD (orange), accuracy is 80.89% and token count is 534.24. For CCoT (light blue), accuracy is 88.50% and token count is 445.91. For CoUT (green), accuracy is 88.40% and token count is 354.46. Additionally, a red bar on the far left shows an accuracy of 91.19% with a token count of 676.85, possibly representing a baseline or alternative method not labeled in the legend. The chart visually emphasizes that CoUT achieves near-parity in accuracy with CCoT while using significantly fewer tokens, and that the red bar (highest accuracy) comes at the cost of the highest token usage. The legend at the bottom confirms the color mapping: red (unlabeled in legend but shown in chart), gray (not used), orange for CoD, light blue for CCoT, and green for CoUT.
